text:
devin_sales: Hey @price_ops — quick heads up. EDU customer (Acme University) is asking for a custom rate + a ratecard version lock. 12mo commit for $200k, procurement insists on v2026-03 and wants the edu_discount line item (not present in v2026-04). Can we do an exception?

alex.s: PricingOps here. We can process exceptions but this needs Deal Desk approval. Are they committing to hosted usage only or a mix with Dedicated?

devin_sales: Mix — about 80% hosted tokens, 20% dedicated reserved at peak. They explicitly want the contract to reference v2026-03 and be grandfathered for the term.

maria_pm: Flag: v2026-04 changes burst pricing and the dedicated overage rules. Locking to v2026-03 may have operational implications if we change billing primitives.

pricebot: [automated] Ratecard v2026-03 currently active. Exceptions permitted under Deal Desk policy v1.2. Reference: https://redwood.example/ratecards/v2026-03 

carol_ops: Ops question: do they expect committed dollars to count toward Dedicated capacity thresholds? If so, we need explicit allocation in contract. Otherwise credits default to hosted usage.

jamie_legal: Legal here. We can add a "ratecard lock" clause. Suggest language: "Ratecard v2026-03 shall apply for the term; any pricing changes will only apply upon mutual written agreement." We'll need procurement redlines.

alex.s: For Deal Desk intake, please provide: 1) final SKUs + dollar split, 2) requested discount % and cap, 3) contract term and start date, 4) any service-level guarantees or fallback models, 5) customer PO.

devin_sales: Ok — summary for intake: SKUs: hosted-text-gen ($160k equiv), dedicated-reserved ($40k equiv). Requested discount: 35% edu discount on list. Term: 12 months starting upon signature. Ratecard: locked to v2026-03 for the term. No forced migration to v2026-04. PO to follow later today.

devin_sales: Proposed contract snippet for Legal/Deal Desk (feel free to redline):

```
Commit: $200000 over 12 months
Allocation:
  hosted_tokens: $160000
  dedicated_reserve: $40000
Ratecard: v2026-03 (locked for term)
Discount: 35% off list for the committed SKUs
Fallback: If capacity constraints occur, customer will be routed to a compatible model variant; latency SLA maintained where possible.
```

alex.s: Good. Submit this as a "Deal Desk Exception Request" with tag `edu-exception` and attach the PO. I'll triage Monday morning. Typical turnaround 48-72h but may be faster if Legal signs off. :thumbsup: 

maria_pm: Note for engineering: if we lock v2026-03, we should schedule backports for any critical runtime patches that change model serving behavior. Ops/infra to confirm feasibility.

carol_ops: Confirmed — we can backport security/critical patches for a locked ratecard term, but maintenance windows will be required. I'll add that to the request.

jamie_legal: I'll wait for the PO and will prepare a redline template including the ratecard lock clause and allocation language. Please cc me on the submission.

devin_sales: Thanks all — I'll submit to Deal Desk now and ping when PO arrives. Tagging @jamie_legal and @alex.s so nothing slips.

dealbot: [system] Deal Desk request created: #DD-7891 (status: pending intake). Link: https://redwood.example/dealdesk/DD-7891

alex.s: Noted. I'll add reviewers from Pricing, Product, and Ops to DD-7891. Expect an internal decision thread after intake review.

devin_sales: Appreciate it. If anyone sees major blockers before intake completes, flag here.

carol_ops: No blockers from infra side at this moment.

maria_pm: I'll keep an eye on potential billing implications and surface them during the DD review.
